title: Unified Pricing & Packaging: Redwood Optimize vNext (PRD + Roadmap + Release Notes)
author: Avery Chen
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the next major iteration of Redwood Optimize (vNext). It is intended for cross-functional stakeholders (product, engineering, sales, finance, and marketing) to align on scope, success metrics, and rollout plan.
overview: Background: Redwood Optimize bundles cost and performance tooling for inference (batching suggestions, caching profiles, quantization recommendations, and quality monitoring). Customers use Optimize to reduce per-token cost and detect quality regressions across model and prompt changes. Objective: Deliver a unified pricing and packaging model for Optimize vNext that supports self-serve users, committed customers (Dedicated), and enterprise Private deployments while enabling clear unit economics and predictable revenue growth.
prd_requirements:
Goals (north-star):
- Reduce average per-token inference cost for typical production workloads by 20% (measured on a benchmark workload).
- Increase adoption of Optimize paid features by 35% of active accounts within 90 days of launch.
- Provide transparent cost impact reporting at token/route/model granularity.

Primary user personas:
- ML Engineer (Platform): wants model+config recommendations and API integrations to apply quantization/batching policies.
- Product Engineer: wants out-of-the-box suggestions and easy SDK hooks to enable caching and batching.
- Finance/Procurement: needs clear pricing tiers and commitment options.

Must-have requirements (MUST):
1) Core APIs: endpoints to submit workload profile, receive batching/quantization recommendations, and apply server-side policy (REST + SDKs).
2) Console: per-route cost breakdown, recommendation preview, and one-click apply for hosted customers.
3) Billing telemetry: fine-grained usage events (recommendation type, savings_estimate, applied boolean) emitted to billing pipeline.
4) Compatibility: support top 10 production models in catalog (e.g., RedLM-3B, OpenLlama-7B, Falcon-40B) and common quantization profiles.
5) Backwards compatibility: default behavior must not change existing customer inference or billing without opt-in.

Should-have (SHOULD):
- Autosuggest rules for PBQ (prefix batching + quantization) per route.
- Integration with rollout policies to A/B recommended settings.

Nice-to-have (COULD):
- Offline batch analysis tool for customers to run local sim and preview savings.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency overhead for applying recommendations must be <5ms p50 for control-plane operations.
- Recommendation service SLA 99.9% availability for hosted control plane.
- Recommendations accuracy: measured savings delta must be within ±15% of actual observed savings in 80% of trials.
design_specs:
High-level architecture:
- Components:
  - Workload Analyzer (WA): lightweight job that ingests sample traffic, computes sequence length distribution, cache hit patterns, and KV-cache reuse metrics.
  - Recommendation Engine (RE): rules + ML scorer that outputs batching window, max_batch_size, quantization_profile_id, and estimated_savings.
  - Apply Service (AS): safe execution of policy changes (API to change model config, enable quantized variant, set batching parameters).
  - Telemetry & Billing Adapter (TBA): emits events to telemetry pipeline and billing.

Interfaces and data contracts (examples):
- POST /v1/optimize/analyze -> { sample_id, route, time_range } -> returns analysis_id (string).
- GET /v1/optimize/recommendations/{analysis_id} -> returns: recommendation_id (string), description (string), savings_estimate_usd (string), expected_latency_change (string), compatibility (comma-separated model ids).

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Safety-first: all Apply operations must be reversible and require a canary rollout for Dedicated/private by default.
- Conservative default recommendations for high-SLO routes to avoid latency regressions.
- Use hybrid rule-based + small ML model for RE to keep inference fast and explainable.

Security & compliance notes:
- Recommendation payloads may include sampled customer telemetry; ensure PII scrubbed and retention matches data-residency policies.
- Private deployments must run RE inside customer VPC/hardened runtime per Private deployment controls.

Acceptance criteria (example table):
- | Criteria | Target | Owner |
  |---|---:|---|
  | p50 apply latency (control plane) | <5ms | eng-platform |
  | Recommendation accuracy (savings error) | ±15% (80% trials) | applied-ml |
  | Console adoption (apply from UI) | 35% of active Optimize users in 90d | product-growth |
roadmap_and_themes:
Quarterly roadmap highlights:
- Q1 2027: Core APIs, console cost breakdown, initial Recommendation Engine supporting RedLM-3B/7B and Open models; beta for Hosted customers.
- Q2 2027: Dedicated commit integration (reserved capacity-aware suggestions), autosuggest rules, and expanded model compatibility to Falcon-40B.
- Q3 2027: Private deployment packaging for enterprise customers + offline batch analysis tool.
- Q4 2027: Quality monitoring regressions & alerting (prompt-level eval integrations) and pricing/packaging v2.

Cross-cutting themes:
- Production-first: defaults must be safe; enable rapid rollback.
- Cost transparency: customers must always see "estimated savings" and the metric math used to compute it.
- Enterprise readiness: permit on-prem RE execution and legal-friendly telemetry options.

KPIs to track post-launch:
- Adoption: % active accounts using at least one Optimize recommendation.
- Savings realization: aggregate monthly USD saved for customers on hosted Redwood.
- Revenue: new revenue from Optimize-paid features and committed contracts.
- Quality: false-positive regression alerts per 1K evals.
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
Pricing principles:
- Value-based pricing: charge based on realized savings and feature set (self-serve vs committed).
- Predictability for enterprise: committed Dedicated/Private customers get discounted pricing tied to monthly saving targets.

Proposed SKUs and tiers:
- Optimize Basic (free tier): cost insights, limited console reports, 1 analysis/month, community support.
- Optimize Pro (pay-as-you-go): $0.0008 per recommendation-evaluation (includes analysis + recommendation), 30-day retention of telemetry, console apply disabled (manual API only). Includes SDK integration.
- Optimize Committed (reserved capacity add-on): starting at $5k/mo commit for up to $X estimated savings baseline; includes automatic apply, faster SLA, and 10% discount on applied savings fees.
- Optimize Enterprise (Private): fixed platform fee + per-seat admin + optional on-prem RE deployment. Custom pricing on contract.

Billing events and metering:
- Metered events: analysis_run, recommendation_evaluated, recommendation_applied, estimated_savings_realized (monthly reconciliation).
- Invoicing: monthly for pay-as-you-go; quarterly/annual for committed contracts with true-up reconciliation.

Packaging notes for go-to-market:
- Self-serve flow: free Basic -> Pro trial (30 days) -> easy upgrade CTA in console.
- Sales-assisted flow: enable Optimize Committed as upsell during Dedicated/Private procurement; include ROI calculator and pilot agreement template.
- Partner motion: include OEM marketplace listing with clear entitlements for partner-managed Dedicated clusters.
release_notes:
Release: Redwood Optimize vNext (2027-01-15)
Summary: Initial public release of Optimize vNext with Analysis API, Recommendation Engine (beta), Console cost breakdown, and Pro tier billing.
What’s new:
- Analysis API (POST /v1/optimize/analyze) to ingest sampled workload and produce analyzers.
- Recommendation Engine v0.9 (rule-based + ML scorer) supporting RedLM-3B, OpenLlama-7B. Provides batching/quantization suggestions with estimated savings.
- Console: per-route/token cost breakdown and "Preview Recommendation" UX with one-click apply for Hosted customers.
- Billing: new metered events (recommendation_evaluated, recommendation_applied). Pro tier billing enabled.
Fixed:
- Improved telemetry schema for sequence-length histograms to reduce storage overhead by 35%.
Known issues & mitigations:
- Falcon-40B support is not available in v0; customers on Falcon see a compatibility warning in the console. Mitigation: add Falcon to compatibility matrix in Q2 2027.
- Estimates for very spiky workloads (95th percentile length > 8x median) can be optimistic. Mitigation: RE flags high-variance workloads and recommends manual review before apply.
Upgrade/rollback notes:
1) Default behavior is opt-in. Hosted customers must click "Apply" in Console or call API.
2) When applying a recommendation, we create an automatic canary (5% traffic for 30 minutes) and monitor latency & error rates; if SLOs degrade, rollback automatically.
3) For Dedicated/private rollout, apply is staged: Canary (5%), Ramp (25%), Full (100%), with manual approval required for private deployments.
Metrics & monitoring added:
- Dashboard: Optimize > Recommendations > Adoption & Savings (new Grafana dashboard).
- Alerts: RE error rate > 1% for 10m, savings_estimate_error_rate > 20% for 1h.
Rollout plan:
- Week 0 (2027-01-15): Launch hosted beta to 10% of eligible accounts.
- Week 2: Open Pro tier to self-serve billing.
- Week 6: Evaluate metrics (adoption, accuracy) and expand to 50% if healthy.
- Q2 2027: Dedicated commit integration and Falcon compatibility.
